subject: Next steps: Clarify infra requirements (SSO / KMS / log retention)
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Molly Chen <molly.chen@finsolve.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — infra constraints that drive Dedicated vs Private

Hi Molly — great to meet you and the team on today's call. Quick recap and requested clarifications so we can recommend the best deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem). Please confirm the items below or flag anything I misunderstood.

Recap / constraints you mentioned:
- SSO: Okta SAML + SCIM provisioning (enterprise Okta tenant).
- KMS: Customer wants to manage encryption keys; preference for cloud KMS with HSM-backed keys (GCP KMS called out).
- Logging: Audit and application logs must be retained for 7 years and be exportable to your SIEM; vendor-hosted long-term storage is restricted.
- Network: Private peering/VPC connectivity is required for production.
- Data residency: US-only.
- Timeline: Pilot in Q3, production by end of Q4.
- Load: Estimated 15 requests/sec peak, ~1.5M tokens/day for initial rollout.

Open questions we need answers for to recommend a deployment and scope the PoC:
1) For KMS/HSM: can you confirm the exact provider (GCP KMS vs Cloud HSM vs third-party HSM appliance) and whether you require external HSM attestation (e.g., FIPS 140-2 Level 3)?
2) For logs: can Redwood forward all inference logs to your SIEM via a secure collector (we support syslog/HTTPS ingestion), or do you require logs to be stored only within your own storage account?
3) For SSO / user provisioning: will SCIM write access be allowed from a vendor-managed service, or must SCIM be proxied through your IdP gateway?
4) Any procurement or security document owners we should loop in now (legal, procurement, InfoSec)?

Next steps I propose:
- You send the security owner contact and a short copy of your KMS/HSM requirements.
- We schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with Diego (SE) to validate network and KMS integration options.
- We prepare a short deployment-options matrix (Attached) that maps each constraint to the recommended mode and implementation effort.

I've attached the deployment-options matrix and a short checklist — Diego will follow with a proposed tech-call slot.

Thanks again,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments:
- deployment-options-matrix.xlsx (summary matrix — Hosted / Dedicated / Private vs each constraint)
- security-checklist.pdf (high-level artifacts we typically request)

From: Molly Chen <molly.chen@finsolve.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinSolve - Security Team <security@finsolve.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — infra constraints that drive Dedicated vs Private

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the items and answering the questions below.

Confirmed:
- SSO: Okta SAML for auth, SCIM for provisioning. We can create a service integration for Redwood but SCIM write calls must be scoped to a service account you will use for provisioning.
- KMS/HSM: We use GCP KMS with HSM-backed keys (Cloud HSM). We require FIPS 140-2 Level 2 minimum; Level 3 is preferred for keys used in signing.
- Logs: All logs must be forwarded into our Splunk instance. We cannot retain long-term logs in a vendor-managed bucket unless we get a contractual carve-out. Short-term vendor caching (24–72 hours) is acceptable if automatically exported.
- Network: Production must be over private VPC peering with MTLS.
- Residency: US regions only.
- Load: Updated estimate after Q2 test: 20 rps peak, ~2M tokens/day.
- Timeline: Pilot target mid-August.

Answers to open questions:
1) KMS/HSM: GCP KMS + Cloud HSM. We will share the KMS project id and a contact.
2) Logs: Redwood must support pushing logs to our Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC) or allow us to pull logs from a customer-owned storage account.
3) SCIM: We will allow SCIM provisioning from a vendor-managed service account (scoped).
4) Security owners: looping in our InfoSec lead (security@finsolve.com) and procurement (procure@finsolve.com).

We think Private VPC looks like the safest path; Dedicated might be possible if we can ensure customer-managed KMS and strict log egress controls.

Molly
Director of Platform Engineering | FinSolve
molly.chen@finsolve.com | +1 (646) 555-0147

Hi Molly / Priya / Jordan — thanks for the details, and appreciate the security team's involvement. A quick technical note ahead of our deep-dive to frame options and highlight integration risk areas.

Summary guidance (high-level):
- Private VPC (recommended):
  - Pros: Full control of KMS (GCP KMS + Cloud HSM) and direct log export to your Splunk collector; can meet 7-year retention via your storage.
  - Cons: Longer lead time for network provisioning; requires customer firewall rules and peering config.

- Dedicated (possible):
  - Requirements: Customer-managed KMS integration (we support CMEK via GCP KMS and Cloud HSM). Network must allow secure connection (VPC peering or VPN) and we must be granted a minimal set of egress routes for log forwarding to your Splunk HEC endpoint.
  - Limitations: Some vendor-side operational telemetry is harder to hide in a hosted Dedicated pool; will need contractual controls and audit reports.

- Hosted API (unlikely for production given requirements):
  - Can work for pilot only if: (a) you accept short-term vendor cache (<=72h) and (b) we can push logs to your Splunk HEC and/or you can pull logs from a customer-owned export bucket. Hosted cannot currently integrate into customer HSM appliances on-prem.

Risk items to confirm before PoC:
1) KMS key rotation responsibilities and whether Redwood will be permitted to call Encrypt/Decrypt using a service account that you provision.
2) Network egress: firewall and NAT rules for our monitoring collectors, and whether MTLS policies can be enforced.
3) Audit artifacts: which compliance artifacts (SOC 2 reports, penetration test summaries) your security team needs in advance. We can supply our SOC 2 Type II report and penetration test summary for the last 12 months.

Attachments: short deployment-options matrix and security checklist for your reviewers. For the deep-dive, I recommend the following agenda: 1) Network topology and peering options (20m) 2) KMS integration patterns and required IAM (20m) 3) Log export/forwarding patterns and SIEM integration (15m) 4) Next steps and pilot SOW (5m).

Proposed slots (PST): Thu 19 Mar 10:00–11:00 or Tue 24 Mar 09:00–10:00. Please confirm which works for you and include any additional technical attendees.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
